model: EVlink Pro AC charging station (Modbus TCP)
applies_to: EVlink Pro AC charging stations (T2S socket, attached cable, and T2S plus domestic socket versions), software 1.1.6 to 1.4.0.
summary: The EVlink Pro AC runs a Modbus TCP server so a building or energy management system can limit its charging current and monitor it. This map covers the pilot and OCPP states, firmware version, the lifebit heartbeat, remote commands, the current setpoint and fallback setpoints, session data, error bitfields, the last four events and the model strings.

addressing.note: The guide says the register table is on base 0, so the printed address goes on the wire unchanged: the current setpoint at 4004 is requested at address 4004.

source.title: EVlink Pro AC Modbus Connectivity Guide
source.revision_date: 2026-03 (cover date; the revision history lists January 2026)
source.pages: printed pp. 9-10 (commands, lifebit, setpoint), pp. 11-14 (registers), pp. 14-15 (data formats), pp. 15-16 (error codes)

notes: Word order: the guide's data-format table defines UINT32 as U32-4321 (high word in the first register), so the uint32 registers are mapped high word first (ABCD).

Left out: the per-phase float32 measurements at 2999-3109 (currents, voltages, active/reactive/apparent power, power factor, frequency). The format table defines both IEEEFloat (F32-4321, high word first) and SwappedFloat (F32-2143) but never says which one the register table's float32 means, so the word order is not stated.

Left out: Energy Active TOT (3203, Wh) and Energy Reactive TOT (3219, kVARh). They are typed int64, and the format table defines two 64-bit layouts (S64-87-21 and S64-21-87) without saying which one int64 means.
The guide's text says the fallback currents are set by writing 4005 and 4006, but the register table marks both read-only and says they are configured in eSetup. They are kept read-only here.
Revision 02 of the guide (March 2023, software 1.2.1) moved addresses 1211-1213 and 4003-4011 up by one; older firmware may still use the old numbers.

The register page says reading an address not in the table returns Illegal data address, while the revision history (revision 04) says reads inside the reserved ranges 2999-3222 and 4000-4079 return 0xFFFF.
Error codes 1.1 to 19.0 and their OCPP equivalents are listed on printed pp. 15-16; the bitfields at 4020/4022 flag the active ones (bit assignment not given).
All values are refreshed once per second.

integration.summary: Connect over Modbus TCP to unit ID 255. Write the current limit in amps to 4004 and keep the lifebit at 4000 cycling so the charger knows the master is alive; read 1 and 150 for state and 4012 for session energy.
integration.enable: The degraded (fallback) setpoints are configured with the eSetup tool. The guide does not say how Modbus is switched on or where the communication timeout is set.
integration.watchdog: With the lifebit active (charger writes 1, master resets it to 0), Modbus counts as lost if the master does not refresh it within the configured communication timeout; the charger then limits to the fallback current in 4005 (single-phase) or 4006 (three-phase). Writing 2 to 4000 deactivates the lifebit.
quirks: 4004 reads 99 until a Modbus master has written a setpoint since start-up.
A setpoint change can take up to 15 s to take effect.
setup: Addresses are 0-based (the table is on base 0).
gotchas: Firmware older than software 1.2.1 (guide revision 02) has addresses 1211-1213 and 4003-4011 one lower.
The lifetime energy counters (3203/3219) are int64 with an unstated word layout, so they are not in this map.

address_note: address = 0-based Modbus wire (PDU) address; documented = as printed in the source.
